transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Time: 15:00 EDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Laura Diaz (Seaboard - Head of AI/ML), Mark Simmons (Seaboard - Head of InfoSec), Ravi Patel (Seaboard - Cloud Architect)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on data residency, logging/retention limits, HIPAA and GDPR applicability for financial services, and evaluation of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options. Next steps: send security docs, schedule technical deep dive, customer to provide sample dataset and compliance checklist.

Topics Covered:
- Data residency requirements (EU, US state-specific restrictions)
- Encryption, KMS/HSM integration, key ownership
- Logging, PII redaction, audit log retention policies
- SOC2/ISO requirements and evidence sharing
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs: latency, cost, data isolation
- Benchmarks and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, you all there?
[00:03] Laura Diaz: Yep, hi Maya, hi Ethan, thanks for doing this.
[00:06] Ethan Park: Morning, afternoon? yeah thanks for carving the time.
[00:09] Mark Simmons: Hi, Mark here from InfoSec. We'll try to be succinct.
[00:12] Ravi Patel: Ravi, cloud, hello.
[00:15] Maya Chen: Great, quick agenda - understand your residency and compliance constraints, current stack, and talk options (hosted, dedicated, private). Then capture next steps, okay?
[00:25] Laura Diaz: Sounds good. We're evaluating for a handful of use cases: internal agent, customer support summarization, and some risk scoring pipelines. Big ask is we cannot have any EU-customer PII leave EU, and for certain B2B accounts we need logs retained only in our environment.
[00:40] Ethan Park: Got it. When you say logs retained in your environment, do you mean all inference logs or just request/response?
[00:48] Mark Simmons: Ideally we'd keep full audit logs but scrub PII after X days. Some regulators in the EU expect data to be resident and auditable within EU boundaries. For a subset of clients we may need on-prem or a VPC private deployment.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Understood. Quick question on threat model - do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) so Redwood never sees unwrapped data?
[01:12] Mark Simmons: Yes, for certain accounts we need key ownership to be ours. We also need proof of encryption at rest and in transit, and we want to review our access to raw transcripts.
[01:22] Ethan Park: That maps to what our Private deployment supports - you can bring your own KMS (BYOK) and run in a VPC with a customer-managed control plane. Dedicated also supports keys and strong isolation but control plane is still managed depending on the contract. Hosted is easiest but less control on key ownership.
[01:38] Ravi Patel: On the Dedicated option, are logs ever replicated to US regions? We have EU-only requirements for some products.
[01:44] Ethan Park: You can pin region and set routing policies; we can prevent cross-region replication. There are a few gotchas - e.g., fallback routing if capacity is constrained could route to another region unless we lock policies. We typically recommend Dedicated with geo-pinning for EU-only workloads.
[02:02] Laura Diaz: How about GDPR subject access and deletion? If a user asks for deletion, does Redwood keep any cache or KV-store entries that could be tied back?
[02:12] Ethan Park: We do have KV cache and prefix caching for performance. For private and dedicated deployments, you can control cache expiry and we can implement stronger policies - purge on demand is possible but needs ops playbook. On hosted, deletion requests are handled per our policy but you don't get direct cache-control.
[02:30] Mark Simmons: Do you retain model training data from our prompts? We need assurances that prompts won't be used to train models.
[02:36] Maya Chen: We do not use customer prompts to further train Open models as part of our hosted offering; we have policy and can provide contractual language. For Private, obviously, you control the environment.
[02:45] Laura Diaz: Can you send the exact language? Our legal will want the clause.
[02:48] Maya Chen: Yes we'll include that in the security pack.
[02:50] [02:50] Ethan Park: Quick architecture note: for Private we deploy a control plane that can be customer-managed or hosted. Models run on dedicated GPU pools in the region. We support KMS integrations (AWS, Azure, or customer HSM) and VPC peering.
[03:08] Ravi Patel: On logs - we need to ensure audit logs cannot be exported except to our SIEM. Does Redwood support log forwarding only to customer endpoints?
[03:16] Ethan Park: Yes, log forwarding via syslog/Kinesis/EventHub etc is supported; you can disable retention on Redwood side if you want. There's often a short buffer for troubleshooting, but for Dedicated/Private we can set that to zero or implement an export-only flow.
[03:30] Mark Simmons: About HIPAA - we have a small business line that touches PHI. Can Redwood sign a BAA and ensure PHI controls?
[03:38] Maya Chen: We have a BAA offering for enterprise customers - typically with Dedicated or Private deployments. Hosted can be supported under strict configurations with contractual controls; we'll need to align on data flows and logging.
[03:51] Laura Diaz: What about SOC2/ISO? We need evidence and possibly penetration test reports.
[03:56] Maya Chen: We'll share SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 artifacts in the security package. We can also provide pen test summaries and detailed architecture diagrams under NDA.
[04:06] Ravi Patel: Bandwidth and latency - our internal apps need sub-200ms for short prompts. How does Dedicated vs Hosted compare?
[04:13] Ethan Park: Hosted is multi-tenant and very fast for most use cases but can have noisy neighbor variability. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable p99 latency; Private on-prem gives lowest network hop latency for internal traffic depending on your infra. We can provide p50/p95/p99 benchmarks for target models.
[04:31] Laura Diaz: On the security questionnaire, there are specific questions about logs retention length and whether you store full request/response payloads. How should we answer those today?
[04:39] Maya Chen: Short answer: Hosted stores minimal logs for 30 days by default with access controls; Dedicated can be configured to retain or not retain and to forward logs; Private keeps logs under customer control. We'll fill in specifics in the security questionnaire.
[04:52] [04:52] Ethan Park: One small transcribing note - our RU'd caching is sometimes called K-V cash in transcripts, haha - it's KV cache.
[04:59] Laura Diaz: Ha, noted.
[05:02] Mark Simmons: Are there restrictions on the types of logs Redwood exposes? For compliance we don't want token-level logs stored outside our environment.
[05:10] Ethan Park: Token-level logs are sensitive. For Dedicated/Private we can suppress token-level traces, or redact them before storage. Hosted by default doesn't expose raw token traces to customers, but we can discuss redaction options.
[05:24] Laura Diaz: For data residency: Can we have an EU-only hosted instance?
[05:28] Maya Chen: Yes, we have regionally isolated hosted clusters in EU that we can pin you to. But again, for ultimate control - Dedicated or Private gives you more guarantees and contractual SLAs around routing and fallback.
[05:40] Ravi Patel: For BYOK, is there any live key usage where Redwood has access to plaintext keys?
[05:45] Ethan Park: No - with KMS integration we perform envelope encryption. Keys stay in your KMS; Redwood only receives ciphertext. With HSM/BYOK we can do a zero-trust setup.
[05:54] Mark Simmons: What about data deletion requests, how fast can you purge caches and logs?
[05:59] Ethan Park: For Private/Dedicated we can build a purge playbook and have an API to request purge; target SLA is 24 hours for caches and 72 hours for backups, but this is something we'll confirm and codify in contract. Hosted may be longer depending on retention.
[06:15] Laura Diaz: Let's talk escalation and audit: if regulator requests logs, do you provide chain-of-custody and attestations?
[06:22] Maya Chen: We provide audit logs and can provide signed attestations and evidence as needed under legal process, especially for Dedicated/Private customers.
[06:30] Ravi Patel: On the technical deep dive - could we run a pilot in EU using Dedicated capacity and see throughput/latency with our sample dataset?
[06:36] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Typical pilot is 4-6 weeks: we provision a small GPU pool, run a defined workload, capture performance and cost metrics, and validate security.
[06:45] Laura Diaz: Cost - can we get a rough estimate for Dedicated pilot and for the full production with geo-pinning?
[06:51] Maya Chen: We'll provide a ballpark in the pricing doc; Ethan will run a preliminary cost model based on your expected QPS and request sizes.
[06:59] Ethan Park: For the pilot we often recommend 2-4 reserved GPUs (A100/available analog) depending on model. We'll estimate after we get sample prompts and usage pattern.
[07:11] Mark Simmons: Any known compliance gaps for EU financial regs?
[07:15] Ethan Park: Nothing fundamental - it's mostly implementation: region pinning, BYOK, log forwarding, and contract language. We do see customers require additional encryption-at-rest attestations which we provide.
[07:26] Laura Diaz: Would Redwood act as a sub-processor under GDPR?
[07:30] Maya Chen: Yes, we are a sub-processor. We'll include the Data Processing Addendum (DPA) that outlines responsibilities, subprocessors list, and deletion procedures.
[07:40] Ravi Patel: One operational question - if something goes wrong in the region and you need to failover, what's the fallback process? We can't have EU data fail over to US without approval.
[07:49] Ethan Park: We can set failover policy to manual approval for those geofenced accounts. That does increase RTO/RPO considerations but is doable.
[07:58] Laura Diaz: Good.
[08:00] Maya Chen: Anything we haven't covered that matters?
[08:03] Mark Simmons: Two things: penetration testing cadence and availability of detailed architecture diagrams for our internal review.
[08:09] Maya Chen: We'll include pen test summary and can provide full diagrams under NDA.
[08:13] Ravi Patel: For the sample dataset, any format preference?
[08:16] Ethan Park: JSONL with redaction markers is best - but send us whatever you have and we'll advise.
[08:22] Laura Diaz: Timeline - we want pilot in June, production Q3. Is that reasonable?
[08:27] Maya Chen: Yes, that's feasible. We'll target pilot start early June pending paperwork.
[08:31] [08:31] Maya Chen: Recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2+ISO docs, DPA and BAA, security questionnaire answers, and a pricing/architecture note. SE deep dive next week. Customer sends sample dataset and control list.
[08:44] Laura Diaz: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[08:47] Mark Simmons: Thanks.
[08:48] Ravi Patel: Thanks all.
[08:50] Maya Chen: Appreciate it, talk soon.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: speaker overlaps minimal, occasional mis-words ("K-V cash" for KV cache), typical auto-transcription punctuation issues.
